quarterly_data.signal: Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian sized the TPU franchise against peers for the first time: the size of our accelerator business, our TPU business, is more than twice that of the next largest hyperscaler. He also gave the return math behind the build: the payback period on AI servers in aggregate is less than two years, and on Google's own silicon is half that, and the majority of Google's infrastructure contracts by total contract value are long-term committed five-year contracts.
quarterly_data.figure: TPU/accelerator business more than twice that of the next largest hyperscaler; AI server payback less than two years and half that on own silicon; majority of infrastructure TCV on long-term committed five-year contracts

quarterly_data.signal: Three silicon types are offered side by side — NVIDIA GPUs, Google's own TPUs, and Google's own Arm processors for running the code that models increasingly generate — in Google's 12th year of building accelerators, with separate parts for training (larger-scale clusters, more cluster connectivity) and for inference (much more disk access). Kurian claimed 2.7 times better price performance for training, 80% better price performance for inference, 30% better price performance for CPUs, and machine-learning run cost 2.5 times better than the number one in the industry, all attributed to top-to-bottom co-design of model and silicon.
quarterly_data.figure: 2.7 times better price performance for training; 80% better price performance for inference; 30% better price performance for CPUs; ML run cost 2.5 times better than the number one in the industry

quarterly_data.signal: TPU systems now go to market three ways: subscription inside Google Cloud, a capital purchase where the customer runs the system in its own data center (HPC sites and capital-markets quant firms that cannot move their data or need to sit near the execution venue), and through neoclouds — Kurian disclosed that Google has set one up with Blackstone to offer TPUs as a neocloud. Hardware sales remove Google's own data-center capex and power/space responsibility and improve free cash flow. Google is pre-positioning inventory with long-term capital purchases so component unit costs are efficient, and pushing customers onto long-term contracts.

Commercial metrics behind Cloud's growth: over 17 product lines, each over $1 billion; more than 2x growth year-on-year in new customer acquisitions and 2x growth quarter-on-quarter and year-over-year in deals over $100 million; when a customer commits to a given amount they typically spend more than 50% more than that. Over 90% of the Fortune 100 use Gemini Enterprise and 90% of the Fortune 100 also use Google for cyber defense; 80% of Google Cloud customers now use its AI products and those that do use 1.8 times as many products, with five-year lifetime value estimated at 1.5 times.
